newsitem.title: USA: Dollar slides on concern about Japan forex policy.
newsitem.headline: Dollar slides on concern about Japan forex policy.

text.p: NEW YORK, Nov 8 - The dollar fell on Friday amid lingering uncertainty about Japan's currency policy, false rumours that President Bill Clinton had been shot and position-squaring before a long holiday weekend.

The dollar had declined sharply versus the yen Thursday after a leading Japanese financial newspaper reported that Eisuke Sakakibara, director general of the Finance Ministry's International Finance Bureau, said the Ministry was not trying to push the yen down further.

Market sentiment remained guarded on Friday even though newly appointed Japanese Finance Minister Hiroshi Mitsuzuka told Reuters his government should not intervene in the currency markets and suggested Japan's interest rates would likely remain low.
The Japanese government has kept official interest rates at rockbottom levels and weakened the yen to help boost economic growth.
Kevin Harris, an international economist at MCM CurrencyWatch, said the dollar slid versus the yen on concerns about Japanese foreign exchange policy.
"These policy changes are intentionally veiled," Harris said. "So, there's good reason to worry about this until we get a lot of clarification both from their statements and from their behaviour."
The dollar was also briefly pressured after talk swept through the foreign exchange market early Friday that President Clinton had been shot.
White House deputy press secretary Barry Toiv put the rumour to rest swifly, noting that the President was in the Oval Office, working.

"There was a slight move downward on the dollar but it quickly dissipated," said Doug Lee, an assistant vice president of foreign exchange at Sakura Bank Ltd. "The denials came out very very quickly."
The dollar tumbled as low as 111.36 Japanese yen and 1.5020 German marks, but late demand in New York for the U.S. currency versus the yen helped erase much of the losses.
In late New York trading, the dollar fetched 111.77 yen and 1.5053 German marks, down from 111.90 yen and 1.5112 marks late Thursday.

Foreign exchange desks in the United States will be thinly staffed for the Veterans Day holiday on Monday. The Treasury bond market will be closed, while stock markets will remain open. Currency traders squared their books ahead of the holiday.
"I think they're nervous about having any kind of positions just because the dollar has been making so many wild swings," said a currency trader at a New York branch of a major European bank.
After the Bank of Canada cut its key bank rate on Friday by 0.25 percentage point to 3.25 percent, the Canadian dollar weakened.
The dollar rose to Canadian $1.3313 from C$1.3292 late Thursday. The British pound slid to $1.6470 from $1.6490. The dollar fell to 1.2653 Swiss francs from 1.2734.
